topStory.headline: H.R. Leaders at SHRM Conference Outline A.I. Workforce Implementation Strategy
topStory.summary:
At SHRM's A.I.+H.I. Project conference in San Francisco, workforce leaders Emily Dickens from SHRM and Miriam Vogel from EqualAI argued that human resources departments hold the key to successful A.I. adoption in organizations, according to SHRM. The speakers stated that H.R. must bridge the gap between high-level A.I. policy discussions and practical workforce implementation.

The presentation highlighted three factors for successful A.I. adoption: governance, workforce readiness, and leadership engagement. Vogel noted that employees will not use A.I. tools unless they believe their organization has thoughtfully considered deployment, monitoring, and evaluation. She warned about emerging gaps across demographics and regions, noting that disparities in access and readiness could deepen existing workforce divides.

The speakers emphasized that A.I. literacy cannot be built through purchasing training programs alone but requires grounding in real workplace applications and peer-to-peer learning. They also suggested that courts, not just legislatures, will shape how A.I. policy is applied through decisions around intellectual property, liability, and data usage.

stories.headline: Opinion: A.I. Reveals Where Learning Was Thin to Begin With
stories.summary: University of Virginia computer science professor Xinyao Yi argues that A.I. has not changed how students learn but has revealed where assessments allowed students to succeed without genuine understanding, according to Inside Higher Ed. Students now submit working code they cannot explain, exposing a gap between producing solutions and comprehending them.
